note: Written steps follow the current console. Videos are dated scripted demonstrations; their source commit is retained in videos.json and layouts may differ. Update recording scripts when UI labels change.

steps.title: Sign in
steps.summary: Sign in to approve changes and manage your devices. Your fleet is the workspace that keeps those devices together. For your first update, follow sign-in, capacity, funding, registration, publishing and deployment. The steps marked optional can wait; set up private access first if your software is confidential.
before: A Sui wallet, or a Google account if Google sign-in is offered.
Funds for the first fleet transaction on the selected network. Connection alone does not require a transaction.
actions: Open the console and click Connect Wallet at the top right.
Pick Slush, your extension wallet or Google, and approve the connection.
On your first visit, choose Create default fleet in the fleet selector and approve the request. A fleet is your device workspace; choose it before continuing.
Choose Get started in the sidebar: it shows your account, short address, the selected network and the next onboarding step.
steps.result: Your account is connected, your fleet is selected, and Get started shows the next step.

steps.title: Enable device capacity
steps.summary: Your plan sets how many devices you can manage. Check for an available place before registering a device. Buying capacity does not add funds for device reports or file storage; those are separate budgets.
before: Have funds for account fees on the network shown in the console. An organization administrator must choose the plan.
actions: Open Device capacity to check how many device places are available.
Open Plans and billing, select a reviewed offer and read its device limit, term, token amount and verified payment recipient.
Approve prepayment from your connected wallet. Wait for verified confirmation before retrying.
Apply the due prepaid payment to activate capacity. This uses the existing subscription balance, with a separate network fee.
Return to Device capacity and verify the new limit.
steps.result: Your organization can manage more devices. Buying capacity does not register devices or install software.

steps.title: Fund device and storage budgets
steps.summary: Add funds so devices can send reports and your team can store software files. Device reports and storage use separate budgets. These payments do not increase your device limit. You review and approve every deposit.
before: Funds for account fees on the network shown in the console. Confirm the account and selected network before funding.
actions: Choose Device and storage budgets in the sidebar.
Enter Deposit (SUI) and click Deposit, then approve. If this build offers Create budget and deposit instead, enter the Initial deposit first.
Later deposits use the Deposit button. Open Device balances, spending limits and withdrawals to cap or withdraw per-device funds.
Optionally click Create storage budget under Storage funding to prepay Walrus storage for uploads and log archives.
steps.result: A Confirmed message and an updated balance show that the deposit succeeded. You can open the confirmation to view its reference.

steps.title: Register a device
steps.summary: Install the SuiFleet client on your device. Then use the public address it gives you to add that device to your fleet. Give it a name your team will recognize. Keep its private key on the device; never paste that key into the console.
before: Available device capacity for your organization. A funded device operating budget does not increase your device limit; check Device capacity or Plans and billing first.
The device's address, printed by suifleet --derive-address /etc/suifleet/device.key on the device.
actions: Choose Devices in the sidebar and click Register by address.
Enter a Device name, paste the Device SUI address and pick the Architecture.
Click Register and approve the transaction.
The device appears in the list. It shows as not yet reporting until its client starts and sends a signed report.
steps.result: A new device row with its name, architecture and address. For one device, skip batch enrollment. Continue with private access only for confidential software, then publish and deploy.

steps.title: Enroll a batch (optional)
steps.summary: Optional for larger fleets: use a list of names and serial numbers instead of entering each device address by hand. Each device gets its own enrollment credential. For your first device, use the registration step and skip this one.
before: A roster (CSV of names and serial numbers), or a single device to pair.
The current app requires you to acknowledge that downloaded credentials are the only copy. Follow the written acknowledgment step even if the recording does not show that checkbox.
actions: Choose Enrollment in the sidebar. Under 1. Enrollment batch policy, set a Quota and Valid for days, then click Create policy.
Under 2. Reserve names and serial numbers, paste a roster CSV (or use Pair one device), optionally pick a Default group, and click Check.

Tick “I understand this download is the only copy of these credentials”, then click Download credentials. This archive is the only copy of the claim keys. Keep it offline, put only each device’s own credential on its private provisioning media, and never include credentials in source control or a shared image. Delete the archive once devices have enrolled.
Under 3. Register claims, click Run pending transactions and approve each transaction. Devices then enroll themselves with suifleet --enroll.
steps.result: Entries move from Reserved to Waiting for device, and to Enrolled when each device claims its record.

steps.title: Private-release access (optional)
steps.summary: Optional for private software: choose which devices may download and open your files. Create a device group, add its devices, then grant that group access. Complete this before publishing confidential software. Skip it for the public example.
before: A group you administer, with the intended device members. Create it on Devices → Device groups before continuing.
actions: Open Access policies and create a named policy.
Choose Group as the recipient type, select the demo group and click Grant decryption.
Approve the transaction. The group appears under granted recipients.
steps.result: Devices currently in the group can request access to the private files. Removing access cannot take back a copy that a device has already decrypted.

steps.title: Publish a version
steps.summary: Add a software version to your library, including the file and the instructions your devices need to install it. Choose Confidential to encrypt private software. Public files are not encrypted and can be read by anyone. Publishing prepares a version for deployment. It does not install it on a device.
before: The software file you want to install, with a separate file for each device platform.
An access policy (Access policies page) naming who may decrypt it, for confidential delivery.
Confidential delivery also requires the build’s encryption service configuration. If unavailable, ask your administrator; do not switch proprietary software to Public.
actions: Choose Software library in the sidebar. The first time, click Set up publishing to create your publisher catalog.
Click Publish version, enter the Component name and Semantic version, and continue.
For each platform choose the Operating system and Architecture, attach the Artifact and, if needed, an Install command.

Under Delivery keep Confidential and choose the Access policy for proprietary software. The recorded example chooses Public (unencrypted) and confirms that its example artifact contains nothing confidential.
Click Review version, then Upload and publish version, and approve the transaction.
steps.result: Version published confirms that the software version is available in your library. You can now choose where to deploy it.

steps.title: Deploy to a device or group
steps.summary: Choose a published version and the devices that should receive it. You can target one device or a group. For a group, you can also keep that version as its target for future checks. After approval, each device checks for the update and reports its result.
actions: For group delivery, on Devices open Device groups and Create group with a Group name, or reuse the group prepared for private access. Skip group setup for a one-device deployment.
For a group, use Manage to Add its intended devices if they are not already members.

In Software library click Deploy this version. Alternatively, choose Deploy software in the sidebar, then Choose or publish a version to open the library. The optional Advanced: deploy a file directly section is for a one-off file without a library entry.

Under Select targets & review select groups or individual devices. Library versions support Make this the groups’ desired version: keep it selected for continuing group convergence, or clear it for a one-shot deployment. Desired state supports groups only; clear individual devices before using it. Review the target count and click Deploy.
Approve the transaction, then open View deployments to follow each device's signed result.
steps.result: Deployment created confirms the request. Wait for device-signed results under Deployments. Applied records installer completion; check application health separately. A first-device pilot can target its individual device with desired state cleared; groups are optional.

steps.title: Run a staged rollout (optional)
steps.summary: Optional for larger fleets: try an update on a small batch before sending it to more devices. Set the health checks and failure limits that must pass before continuing. You must return and approve each next batch; the rollout does not advance on its own.
before: A published library version for the target device platform.
Named devices or groups to divide into batches. Configure client reporting. Admission candidates are not proof a device is online; post-apply health gates progression.
actions: Choose Rollouts and open Create a gradual rollout.
Choose Published library version and platform. Add named devices or groups to each cohort (batch); each device can appear in only one batch.
Choose the pace, observation period, minimum reports and failure threshold. Select Review rollout, check the exact plan, then Confirm creation in wallet. Creation starts no devices.

Select the saved rollout, choose waiting devices and approve Check device health and continue. Empty selection checks health without new grants. Return to approve later checks and subsequent batches; closing the browser stops coordination.
Use Pause to stop new starts, Resume to allow further checks, or Abort permanently. Give an audit reason; updates already allowed to start may finish.
steps.result: Creation leaves devices waiting. The demonstration creates and pauses a plan without admitting devices; it does not claim healthy rollout completion. Actual progress requires admitted devices, verified update results and current health reports.

steps.title: Choose fleet settings
steps.summary: Choose how often devices check for updates and report their health. Review the estimated cost before saving. Saving these settings does not add funds; check the device budget separately.
before: A selected fleet and its device operating budget.
actions: Open Fleet settings and choose a device reporting interval.
Review the estimate, then click Save settings and approve.
Open Device and storage budgets to review the balance separately. Saving settings does not fund the budget.
steps.result: The settings are saved. Devices pick them up the next time they check for changes.
